author: rdc-rfc1-author-c (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: The status latch is cleared by rst_b_n and by a two-flop-synchronised copy of rst_a_n, so a source-domain reset clears the status, and the fault path stays inside a two-flop synchroniser.

author_reading.rationale: The status latch is cleared by the destination reset and by the synchronised source reset, so a source-domain reset clears the status with it.

labels.rationale: The status latch is cleared while the synchronised source reset (ra_b_q) is asserted, so a source reset reaches the destination. Only a two-cycle transient remains, and it settles within the sequence.

labels.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
labels.rationale: The sticky status clears only after the destination samples source reset as a level. The SDC gives no minimum assertion width or raw release timing, so the destination could miss a source reset or see the reset and fault paths in different cycles.
labels.suspected_flaw: The guard combines an asynchronous reset and a sampled synchronous clear, which can obscure the distinct control roles in static analysis.

settlement.rationale: A is right on the verdict. B's concerns are a source reset shorter than the synchroniser can see (the generic minimum-pulse obligation) and the mixed guard, which is a legal synchronous clear. The class follows the author: the rfc1-c03 lookalike for reset-domain crossings. RDC-019 may report the sampled rst_a_n.

adjudication.by: rdc-rfc1-adjudicator (Claude Opus 5.5), policy decision after the score
adjudication.reason: the source-reset clear of the sticky status samples rst_a_n as a level in clk_b, so it relies on an undeclared minimum assertion width; RDC_WORKFLOW: an undeclared contract blocks any claim about reset pulse behaviour
